chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'at ibn Mihran, who said:

'Abd Salih (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Sama'at! They believed upon their beds and they are scaring me. But, by Allah! It has been so that in the world and whatever was in it there was only one (person) who worshipped Allah, and had there been anyone else along with him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would have Added him in, where He is Saying:'
[16:120] Surely Ibrahim was a community, obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not from the Polytheists.

So it remained like that for as long as Allah so Desired. Then Allah Comforted him with Isma'il and Is'haq, and thus they became three. But, by Allah! The Momineen have always been few and the people of disbelief numerous. Do you know why that is so?' So I said, 'I do not know, may I be sacrificed for you!' So he said: 'They were made a comfort for the Momineen, to whom they pour out what is in their hearts, so they find rest in that and tranquility therein.'

key_terms.آنَسَهُ: Anasahu — He comforted him and granted him intimate companionship; Allah relieving the solitude of Ibrahim (AS) through righteous companions
key_terms.أُمَّةً: Ummah — community or nation; here applied uniquely to Ibrahim (AS) alone, signifying that a single sincere worshipper can constitute an entire community in the sight of Allah
key_terms.أُنْساً: Uns — intimate companionship, comfort, and solace; the quality of being a trusted confidant and source of relief to another
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: Ju'iltu fidak — 'May I be made your ransom' — a classical Arabic expression of utmost reverence, devotion, and self-sacrifice directed toward the Imam
key_terms.حَنِيفًا: Hanif — one who is upright and inclined exclusively toward pure monotheism, having turned away from all falsehood and shirk
key_terms.عَبْدٌ صَالِحٌ: Abd Salih (the Righteous Servant) — an honorific title used for Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kazim (AS), the seventh Imam
key_terms.قَانِتًا: Qanit — one who is devoutly and humbly obedient to Allah in sustained, dedicated worship
key_terms.يَبُثُّونَ: Yabutthhun — to pour out and confide; the act of sharing the innermost burdens and concerns of one's heart with a trusted companion

ai.seo_question: Why are true believers always few in number, according to Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), referred to by the honorific 'Abd Salih, addresses his companion Sama'at ibn Mihran, lamenting that certain people profess faith outwardly while causing fear to the Imam. He establishes the rarity of true belief through the example of Ibrahim (AS), who alone constituted an entire ummah in his worship of Allah before Allah comforted him with the companionship of Isma'il and Is'haq. The Imam reveals that the perpetual smallness in the number of true believers is by divine wisdom, as others are appointed as a source of intimate companionship through whom believers may pour out their innermost concerns and thereby attain rest and tranquility.

en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan from Sama’a ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“A virtuous servant (of Allah) (a.s.) said to me, ‘O Sama’a, they (pretending Shi’a) found their belief in their beds and they (attempt) to frighten me (ignoring al-Taqiyah). By Allah, once of the whole world and all that is therein there was only one person who worshipped Allah. Had there been anyone else, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, would have mentioned him with him in His words,
‘Abraham was, certainly, a nation, (in terms of having a whole culture and tradition) obedient and upright person. He was not a pagan.’ ( 16 : 120 )

“Time passed as Allah willed. Allah then provided him comfort with Isma’il and Ishaq and they numbered three. By Allah, believers are very few and unbelievers (people of imperfect belief) are many. Do you know why that is?’ I said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I do not know.’ The Imam said, ‘They (less perfect believers) have become a source of comfort for the believers who spread their secrets to the hearts (of less perfect believers) to find relief and in this they do find relief.”
